name: Question 5
problem:
Let ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfy the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=A\text{ }x(t)$ and ${x}_{p}(t)$ satisfy the inhomogeneous system
${x}^{′}(t)=A\text{ }x(t)+f(t).$
Which of the following is **always** a solution of the same inhomogeneous system?

- $-5\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$
- $2\cdot {x}_{1}(t)-7\cdot {x}_{2}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$
- ${x}_{2}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$
worked_solution:
Recall that if ${x}_{h}(t)$ satisfies a homogeneous linear system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution to an inhomogeneous linear system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t),$ then ${x}_{h}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$ is also a solution to the same inhomogeneous system.

Additonally, the *linearity principle* for systems of linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) states that if ${x}_{1}(t),$ ${x}_{2}(t),…,{x}_{k}(t)$ are solutions to a homogeneous linear system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ then any linear combination 

$$
{c}_{1}{x}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{x}_{2}(t)+⋯+{c}_{k}{x}_{k}(t)
$$

with ${c}_{1},{c}_{2},…,{c}_{k}\in R$ is also a solution of the same homogeneous system. 

With that in mind, let's examine the given expression.

- Option I is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination 

$$
{x}_{h}(t)=-5\cdot {x}_{1}(t)
$$

is a solution to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ according to the linearity principle. Thus, 

$$
{{-5\cdot {x}_{1}(t)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{h}(t)}+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

is a solution to our inhomogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).$

- Option II is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination 

$$
{x}_{h}(t)=2\cdot {x}_{1}(t)-7\cdot {x}_{2}(t)
$$

is a solution to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ according to the linearity principle. Thus, 

$$
{{2\cdot {x}_{1}(t)-7\cdot {x}_{2}(t)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{h}(t)}+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

is a solution to our inhomogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).$

- Option III is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination 

$$
{x}_{h}(t)={x}_{2}(t)
$$

is a solution to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ according to the linearity principle. Thus, 

$$
{{{x}_{2}(t)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{h}(t)}+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

is a solution to our inhomogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II and III".

Question 5

Let x1(t) and x2(t) satisfy the homogeneous system x′(t)=A x(t) and xp(t) satisfy the inhomogeneous system x′(t)=A x(t)+f(t). Which of the following is always a solution of the same inhomogeneous system?

  1. −5⋅x1(t)+xp(t)
  2. 2⋅x1(t)−7⋅x2(t)+xp(t)
  3. x2(t)+xp(t)
a
I, II and III
b
III only
c
I only
d
I and II only
e
II only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if xh(t) satisfies a homogeneous linear system x′(t)=Ax(t) and xp(t) is a particular solution to an inhomogeneous linear system x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t), then xh(t)+xp(t) is also a solution to the same inhomogeneous system.

Additonally, the linearity principle for systems of linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) states that if x1(t), x2(t),…,xk(t) are solutions to a homogeneous linear system x′(t)=Ax(t), then any linear combination c1x1(t)+c2x2(t)+⋯+ckxk(t) with c1,c2,…,ck∈R is also a solution of the same homogeneous system.

With that in mind, let's examine the given expression.

  • Option I is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination xh(t)=−5⋅x1(t) is a solution to the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t) according to the linearity principle. Thus, −5⋅x1(t)⏟xh(t)+xp(t) is a solution to our inhomogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).

  • Option II is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination xh(t)=2⋅x1(t)−7⋅x2(t) is a solution to the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t) according to the linearity principle. Thus, 2⋅x1(t)−7⋅x2(t)⏟xh(t)+xp(t) is a solution to our inhomogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).

  • Option III is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination xh(t)=x2(t) is a solution to the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t) according to the linearity principle. Thus, x2(t)⏟xh(t)+xp(t) is a solution to our inhomogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II and III".
